source: Cox & D'Antonio 3e Appendix A, PDF pages 532-536 (printed pp. 475-479)
about: The hundred and sixty-one rows of "Appendix A: Table of absorption coefficients", printed over five pages under twenty-two bold group headings: curtains or drapes, variation with draping, cotton curtains, carpet, other floors, theatre seating unoccupied, seating occupied, standing audience, miscellaneous, wood, concrete, bricks and blocks, plaster, plasterboard, glazing, wools and foam, ballast, microperforated absorber, diffusers, green wall systems, and two groups of top soil, one by vegetative cover and one by moisture content. Columns as printed: "Material" and, under "Frequency (Hz)", 125, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000. Every one of the 966 cells holds a number: no empty cell, no dash, no word. There is no mounting column and no thickness column, because where a thickness, a density or a cavity depth matters the page puts it in the name, and the names are kept as printed, centimetres, millimetres and kilograms per square metre included. Five groups head a block of rows that are only a condition, a cavity depth or a percentage, and those rows are held with the heading as the name and the printed row as the variant, because "20%" on its own is not a material. The appendix has no caption, no table number, no prose above it and no footnote under it. Its credits are per row: a superscript number on the material name, one or two of them, keyed to the list of twenty-nine references printed on PDF page 537 (printed p. 480), and the row holds that credit as the short form of the reference it points at, which is what makes this appendix a compilation of twenty-nine sources rather than one measurement campaign. Two rows cite in words instead of a superscript, "average from References 1 and 16" and "see Reference 18", and are credited the same way; the twelve top soil rows carry the credit their bold group heading prints once, reference 29, and each holds it. Four rows carry no credit at all: the cork on solid backing, the anechoic chamber wedges, the 50 mm wood and the polyurethane foam. Four rows are printed with three decimals where the rest of the page prints two, and the anechoic wedge row is 0.997 in every band. The page prints a standing audience above 1 at 1 kHz, 2 kHz and 4 kHz and a sheep wool absorbent above 1 at 4 kHz, which is what a reverberation-room coefficient does and not a misreading.
